newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold softer, Indian demand slowly emerging.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold softer, Indian demand slowly emerging.

text.p: Dubai gold prices fell marginally in the week, adding to the momentum of Indian import demand ahead of the Indian festival season, Dubai traders said on Sunday.

Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar (TT) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat imported gold -- was quoted by wholesalers on Sunday at 5,255 UAE dirhams ($1,431.88), a fall of five dirhams on the week while 10 gram pieces were assessed at 449 dirhams.
TT bars in Bombay, a barometer of the profitability of the Dubai-India trade route, were at $1,677 while international spot bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $380.00-50.
The Gulf emirate is the main feed supplier into India which is on course this year to consumer 500 tonnes of the yellow metal, making it the world's single largest gold market.

October and November usually sees a strong pick up in Indian demand as goldsmiths and families prepare for the Hindu festival of Diwali and the country's second marriage season which runs from November through to April.
"Demand is steady, no particular improvement...the lower prices should attract buying but at the moment there is no rush," a Dubai trader said.
Dubai traders highlighted this year's strong monsoon rains across the subcontinent as bullish for the Dubai bullion market because of the improved chances of a good cash crop.
Silver was quoted in Dubai at $158 a kilo and $192 in Bombay.
-- Steven Swindells, Dubai Newsroom, +971 4 6071255. ($1=3.67 UAE dirhams)
